rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN PROVISIONS IN REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to modify certain provisions in the Code to strengthen the SK. It was filed upon the request of the Sangguniang Kabataan National Federation. The bill will, among others: (1) grant the SK a twenty percent (20%) share in the general fund of the barangay; (2) grant SK members, other than the chairman, an honoraria of not less than Three Hundred Pesos (P300.00), which will be equitably based on their attendance at the regular and special sessions of the sanggunian; and (3) allow the mayor to fill-up the vacancies in the sanggunian, other than for the position of Chairman, by the appointment of a replacement recommended by SK concerned.

rows.abstract: There is a need to increase the current authorized number of generals/flag officers in the AFP due to the following reasons:  (1) The present structure organizational structure of the AFP under the Modernization Program requires the more Generals/Flag Officers in the AFP that what is currently authorized. rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE RIGHTS OF PATIENTS AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: "Magna Carta of Patient's Rights." Rationale:  In the Philippines, there is yet a law to be created to protect, promote and depend the rights of patients.  We hear horrifying stories of patients who died or are further injured in hospitals as a result of negligence and incompetence of their supposed healers.  The Professional Regulatory Commission confirmed increasing complaints of medical malpractice numbering more than a hundred as of 1993. The cases include lack of skills, foresight and diligence, misdiagnosis, wrong medication, wrong blood transfusion, adverse effects of anaesthesia and medicine prescribed and administered by health care providers. It is imperative that health authorities, hospital owners and health care providers mustt recognize and promote patients rights.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-08-27

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A FIVE-YEAR EMERGENCY SCHOOLBUILDING PROGRAM APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is the declared policy of the State to establish, maintain, and support a complete, adequate and integrated system of education relevant to the needs of the people society. Towards this end, it is imperative that there be a complete elementary school in every barangay and a complete high school in every town, in order that primary and secondary education be made available and accessible to all citizens in all geographic areas of the country.  In the choice of location of school buildings, the economics principle of comparative advantage shall always be adhered to. The bill provides for an Emergency School building fund amounting to 15 billion pesos which will be released and utilized for a period of five years.  The Five-Yeaar School Building Program targets to eliminate the classroom shortages for a definite period of time.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-08-27

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8545, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `EXPANDED GOVERNMENT ASSISTANCE TO STUDENTS AND TEACHERS IN PRIVATE EDUCATION ACT' PROVIDING FOR AN EXPANDED VOUCHER OR COUPON SYSTEM IN SECONDARY AND TERTIARY EDUCATION AND APPROPRIATINGFUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: The passage of the Expanded Government Assistance to Students and Teachers in Private Education (GASTPE) in 1998 offers many opportunities for the poor students who cannot afford to study in private schools by providing a financial assistance through the tuition fee supplements and education service contracting scheme. Through the GASTPE law, the system of voucher system in tuition fee payment had been introduced. However, there is a need to further improve the system and increase the amount of assistance to students-grante es by amending some sections of the Expanded GASTPE law so that it can become more responsive to the needs of the students and the schools.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-08-27

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AN EMERGENCY MEASURE TO ALLEVIATE THE PLIGHT OF COCONUT FARMERS ADVERSELY AFFECTED BY LOW PRICES OF COPRA AND OTHER COCONUT PRODUCTS AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The proposed EMERGENCY MEASURE PROGRAM shall consist of the following projects:  1. Income supplement projects for coconit farmers; 2. Marketing assistance to coconut farmers; 3. Direct buying of copra at a threshhold price; and 4. Income support onregular sales of copra and whole nuts.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-08-27

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING PRE-SCHOOL EDUCATION, INCREASING THE MONTHLY COMPENSATION OF DAY CARE WORKERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Pre-school Development Act of 2001". Rationale: Child educators agree that starting educators at pre-school age has substantial benefits to the learner and to society. By contributing to better academic performance, pre-schooling helps reduce the number of repeaters, hence we cut back on educational expenditure. > It is hereby declared to be the policy of the State to provide for a unversal early childhood or pre-school education that promotes effective social, intellectual and skills stimulation and value-formation for children from 3-5 years old with the end-view of amply preparing them for formal elementary schooling.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-08-27

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLES 215 AND 216 OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED, BY UPGRADING THE SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND RETIREMENT BENEFITS OF LABOR ARBITERS AND THE COMMISSIONERS OF THE NATIONAL LABOR RELATIONS COMMISSION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Since they perform an important part in the maintenance of industrial peace and in the adjudication of justice in the workplace, it is fitting that Labor Arbiters enjoy equality in rank with judges of the Municipal Trial Courts (MTC). Appropriate retirement benefits must likewise be accorded them to enable them to enjoy the fruits of government service long after they have been served it with their best years.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-08-27

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE THE PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION OF THE NATIONAL HERITAGE, THE CREATION OF A NATIONAL HERITAGE COMMISSION AND PROVIDING PENALTIES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "National Heritage Act of 2001". Rationale: Knowing our heritage would serve as an anchor amidst the chaos that modernization brings.  By preserving our heritage, we keep our integrity as a people, for our heritage is a foundation upon which we canbuild our present, as well as our future. Heritage plays an important role in national destiny, only by knowing our collective strength as a people can we be prepared to meet the challenges posed by globalization. Towards this end, a NATIONAL HERITAGE COMMISSION is hereby created and tasked to establish national principles, standards and policy for the identification, recording and management of heritage resources, among others.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-08-27

rows.author: D066
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING DUAL CITIZENSHIP TO AMERICANS AND OTHER FOREIGN CITIZENS WHO ARE FORMER FILIPINOS OR OF FILIPINO ANCESTRY UNDER CERTAIN CONDITIONS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Dual citizenship is hereby authorized for former Filipinos who acquired American citizenship or any other foreign citizenship, or being a descendant and/or of Filipino ancestry; Provided, however, that their country grants a reciprocal right to Filipino citizens similarly situated; Provided, further, That these Filipino expatriates will register their intent to reacquire, or acquire, as the case maybe, their Filipino citizenship with the Bureau of Immigration expressing therein their loyalty and allegiance to the Republic of the Philippines.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04720

Candidates holding elective office - Any elective official, whether national or local, running for any office other than the one which he is holding in a permanent capacity [, except for President and Vice President, ] shall be considered ipso facto resigned from his office upon the filing of his certificate of candidacy."

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 717, ENTITLED `PROVIDING AN AGRARIAN REFORM CREDIT AND FINANCING SYSTEM FOR AGRARIAN REFORM BENEFICIARIES THROUGH BANKING INSTITUTIONS'
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to correct the decline in agricultural production loans by REDIRECTING the use of the Agri-Agra Fund to favor the small farmers. The proposed amendment to PD No. 717 reads:  TO INVEST OR DEPOSIT THEIR LOANABLE FUNDS FOR AGRICULTURAL AND AGRARIAN REFORM CREDIT WITH GOVERNMENT FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS AND RURAL BANKS FOR THE PURPOSE OF RE-LENDING SUCH LOANABLE FUNDS TO FARMERS AND AGRARIAN REFORM BENEFICIARIES. TO PROMOTE A FUNCTIONAL TIE-UP BETWEEN COMMERCIAL BANKS AND RURAL BANKS,ALL LOANS OF RURAL BANKS REDISCOUNTED WITH COMMERCIAL BANKS SHALL BE DEEMED AS COMPLIANCE WITH P.D. 717.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ABSOLUTELY PROHIBITING DISCRIMINATION AGAINST WOMEN IN ALL MATTERS PERTAINING TO EMPLOYMENT, PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Consistent with this constitutional mandate, the attached bill seeks to prohibit absolutely any act of employer or any person acting on behalf of the employer from discriminating, directly or indirectly, against female employees or workers - or giving preference to male workers - in all matters pertaining to employment or employment opportunities and employment benefits.  The prohibited act shall include announcements, publications or advertisements of any kind or any form that would have the effect of denying women equal employment opportunities on account of their being women.

rows.abstract: This piece of legislation is designed to grant landowners the right to suspend payment of real property taxes if he is deprived of possession of his property because his landholding is occupied by squatters. Stated otherwise, a landowner may not beobligated and required to render payment of the land tax as long as he is able to establish that his land is occupied.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 39 (A)(1) OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 226 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS INVESTMENT CODE OF 1987, AS AMENDED AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill proposes to extend the maximum period for the income tax holiday offered to especially desirable investors from eight (8) to twelve (12) years, subject to the approval of the Secretary of Finance, upon compliance with certain conditions. This extension merely tries to align the Philippines' income tax holidays to match that of our neighboring countries.  By keeping pace with the incentives being offered by other countries, we stand a sufficiently even chance of attracting investmentsand partners that will be crucial in our drive for development.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Our country is haunted by environmental problems which is multi-faceted. Among them are forest denudation, unabated illegal fishing which destroys marine life, loss of soil fertility, water and air pollution and inadequate water disposalsystem, to name a few. These problems deprive the future generations of a health environment, all because of economic development. These geo-political and economic developments uerscore the urgent need for a surveillance and monitoring system to arrest the emerging threat to our national security and environment and prevent unredeemable losses.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING HARBOR PILOTAGE SERVICES AND THE CONDUCT OF HARBOR PULOTS IN ALL PORTS IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR RELATED PURPOSES
rows.abstract: It is hereby organized by the State that pilotage service in an inherent function of the Philippine Ports Authority (PPA) as it plays vital and complementary role in the efficient operation of ports.  It is therefore its policy to regulate, controland supervise pilotage services and the conduct of pilots in all ports in the country to attain the following objectives: > a)  To ensure the safety of port facilities, vessels and their passengers and cargoes; b) To ensure efficient pilotage serviceat all times, rationalize charges therefor and professionalize harbor pilots; and c) To foster competition in the provision of pilotage services.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ADDITIONAL RETIREMENT BENEFITS TO MEMBERS OF THE JUDICIARY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO, 910, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is of common knowledge that the remuneration accorded to the Justice of the Supreme Court and Court of Appeals and other members of the Judiciary is indecently low.  In response to the call of duty in the administration of justice, most of them have had to forego lucrative opportunities elsewhere. The existing retirement laws, foremost of which is Republic Act No. 910, as amended, are unresponsive to the rapidly changing economic conditions. The proposed bill seeks to upgrade these retirement benefits and redefine the retirement condition on the length of service to the government.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND ARTICLE 217 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE MAKING THE FAILURE TO LIQUIDATE CASH ADVANCE WITHIN THE PERIOD PROVIDED THEREIN A PRIMA FACIE PROOF OF MALVERSATION
rows.abstract: Section thirteen of Article 217 of the Revised Penal Code is hereby amended to add another paragraph to read as follows: > "In addition, the failure of a public officer or employee, who was previously granted a cash advance, to liquidate the same after the purpose for which it was given has been served within the following periods shall be prima facie proof of malversation or misappropriatio n of the fund he received, to wit:  >1. Salaries, wages, etc. - within 5 days after each 15th day/end ofthe month pay period. 2. For petty operating expenses and field operating expenses - within 20 days after the end of the year. 3.  For special operations, and operating expenses or purchases of supplies, materials and the like in an amount exceedingg P100,000 - 20 days after the completion of the operation or after the delivery and acceptance of the supplies, materials and the like. 4. For Local travel - within 15 days upon return to his official station. 5. For foreign travel - within 60 days
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-08-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING THE APPROPRIATION, ENCROACHMENT, REGISTRATION AND TITLING OF CREEKS, ESTEROS, STREAMS, CANALS, RIVER BANKS AND OTHER PUBLIC WATERWAYS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Land in urban areas has become so scarce that even small spaces of about 60 square meters have become invaluable. Urban centers have become so crowded that every available space are being encroached upon and titled to the extent that evencanals, streams, esteros are being filled up and built over, regardless of the fact that these are properties of the state, is inalienable and acquisition thereof is fraudulent. This bill seeks to provide penalties to those unscrupulous persons whoexploit this situation. Penalizing such registrants shall serve as a deterrent to these malefactors to prevent or curtail their anomalous acts of titling these waterways.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-08-27

rows.abstract: "Anti-Influence Peddling Act."  It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in influence peddling which is hereby defined as the act of representing oneself, either orally or in writing, as being able, whether real or imagined, to influence, facilitate or assist another person having some business, transaction, application, request or contract with the government in which a public official or employee has to intervene. >  Penalties for Violation. - Any person who engages in influence peddlingas defined by this Act shall be punished by imprisonment of not more than six (6) years or a fine not exceeding One Hundred Thousand (P100,000.00), or both, and disqualificatio n to hold public office.
